The nickel-base single crystal superalloy PWA 1480 is a candidate blading material for the advanced turbopump development (ATD) program of the space shuttle main engine (SSME).
In advanced liquid propellent rocket engines, the turbine blades are subjected to severe thermal gradients, centrifugal loads, and vibratory loads.
The single crystal superalloy PWA 1480 is grown along the low modulus [001] crystal orientation to improve thermal fatigue resistance.
Unless a seed crystal is used, the secondary crystal orientation [010] tends to be randomly oriented with respect to the geometry of the turbine blade.

Cubic single crystal materials like PWA 1480 exhibit anisotropic elastic behavior, so the stresses developed within the material are likely to be affected by the secondary crystallographic orientation.
Temperature-dependent elastic constants and the thermal coefficient of expansion for single crystal PWA 1480 were determined by Pratt & Whitney under a NASA contract.
The elastic stiffness matrices for different secondary orientation angles were computed using the simplified method of Liebermen and Zirinsky.
The finite-element model of the square plate consisted of 500 8-noded, isoparametric elements.
For the case of a thermal gradient through the thickness of the plate, the secondary orientation angle of 0° minimized thermal stresses, while the angle of 45° maximized the thermal stresses.
The variations in the stress components with the secondary orientation angle were dependent on the type of loading (mechanical, thermal, or combined) imposed on the plate.

The elastic stresses developed within the single crystal PWA 1480 plate were computed with elastic finite-element stress analysis for each combination of loading condition and secondary orientation angle.
The commercially available MARC code was used to conduct the elastic stress analyses.
The primary orientation of the square plate was assumed to be along the [001] crystallographic direction.
The secondary crystallographic orientation was offset with respect to the geometric axes of the square plate from 0° to 90° in increments of 10°.
The square plate had a side length of 25.4 mm and a thickness of 3.2 mm.
